title: Specimens
purpose: Find specimens, aliquots and derivatives, see what is on hand and where each one is, export the result, and print labels.
summary: Find specimens, aliquots and derivatives, see what is on hand and where each one is, export the list and print labels.

tasks.title: Open a specimen you have in hand
steps: Scan or type its whole ID in Find specimen ID in the top bar. The record opens.

tasks.title: Find specimens
steps: Type part of a specimen ID, participant code or collection code in [[Search]].
Narrow with [[Status]], [[Specimen type]] or [[On hold]], or open [[More filters]], then select [[Apply]].

tasks.title: Print labels
steps: Tick the specimens on this page.
Select [[Print labels]] and check the preview.

tasks.title: Register a specimen
steps: Select [[Register specimen]]. To register many at once, use Imports.

good_to_know: Specimen IDs are opaque. They never contain a location, participant, study or date, and are never reused.
Without filters the list includes exhausted, disposed and distributed specimens.
A typed participant or box code that does not exist shows no rows, never an unfiltered list.
[[Export CSV]] downloads exactly what the current search, filters and sort show.

sections.title: Who can use it
paragraphs: Every role (admin, manager, technician, viewer) can open the list, search it, export it and print labels. Register specimen appears only for admin, manager and technician; a viewer sees a read-only list. Every specimen is shown to every role; there is no per-study or per-participant restriction.

Specimen IDs are opaque numbers assigned by the system when a specimen is registered, such as VP-000123. They do not contain a location, participant, study or date, and they never change or get reused.

sections.title: Finding a specimen
paragraphs: Find specimen ID in the top bar is the quickest way to open one specimen, for example after scanning a label. It trims spaces, ignores capitals and needs the whole ID (VP-000123); a match opens that specimen's record. If no specimen has that ID, you return to this list with the message “No specimen has ID …” and the text you typed placed in Search, so a partial ID can still match. An empty entry just opens this list.

Search on this page matches part of the specimen ID, participant code or collection code, ignoring capitals. Without any filter every specimen is listed, including exhausted, disposed and distributed ones.

sections.title: Filters
paragraphs: Status, Specimen type and On hold are always visible; the rest sit under More filters, which opens by itself when one of them is in use. Active filters are shown as chips you can remove one at a time. Filters combine with each other (all must match).

Participant code and Box code are typed, not picked: type the exact code (any capitals). A code that does not exist makes that filter invalid. When any filter is invalid the page shows “These filters cannot be applied” and no rows at all, never an unfiltered list, so correct or clear the filter.

items.label: Status
items.description: Any status, Available (some material on hand), Exhausted (used up, nothing left), Disposed (disposal recorded) or Distributed (sent out of the repository in a shipment and not returned).

items.label: Specimen type
items.description: One specimen type from the catalogue, shown by code.

items.label: On hold
items.description: Any, Yes (has an unreleased hold of any kind: disposal, use or all-use, including holds placed by another workflow) or No.

items.label: Specimen container
items.description: The vessel type the specimen is held in.

items.label: Participant code
items.description: Specimens from one coded participant, for example P-000123.

items.label: Collection
items.description: Specimens in one collection.

items.label: Unit
items.description: Specimens measured in one unit of amount.

items.label: Box code
items.description: Specimens currently in one box. Checked-out and unplaced specimens are not in any box.

items.label: Checked out
items.description: Yes lists specimens that are out of storage now; No excludes them.

items.label: In storage
items.description: Yes lists specimens that occupy a storage position; No lists those without one, which includes checked-out specimens and specimens never placed.

sections.title: Columns, sorting and paging
paragraphs: Click Specimen ID, Status, Type, Amount, Collected or Registered to sort; click again to reverse. The default order is by specimen ID, and ties keep a stable order. Choose 25, 50 or 100 rows per page (default 25). Collection and Registered are hidden until you show them. The column menu shows or hides every column except Specimen ID and the selection box.
Amounts are exact decimals with their unit, for example 0.5 mL, never rounded. The amount shown is the balance of the amount ledger on the specimen's record.

items.label: Specimen ID
items.description: The opaque ID; opens the specimen's record. Always shown.

items.label: Status
items.description: Available, Exhausted, Disposed or Distributed, plus On hold when any hold is active.

items.label: Type
items.description: The specimen type name (for example Plasma).

items.label: Amount
items.description: Amount on hand with its unit. Sortable.

items.label: Participant
items.description: The participant code, or a dash. Codes only; no names are held.

items.label: Collection
items.description: The collection code, or a dash.

items.label: Location
items.description: The full storage path of its position. If it is out of storage in someone's hand (checked out, or returned and not yet stored) it says Checked out, with a clock of how long it has been out of storage; a distributed specimen says Distributed: outside the repository; otherwise Not in storage (never placed, or disposed).

items.label: Custodian
items.description: The person who currently holds responsibility for it; Outside the repository while it is distributed.

items.label: Collected
items.description: When it was collected, in repository time. Sortable; newest first on first click.

items.label: Registered
items.description: When it was registered in the system. Sortable; newest first on first click.

items.label: Register specimen
items.description: Admin, manager and technician. Opens the form that registers one new specimen. Many at once are registered through Imports.

items.label: Export CSV
items.description: Downloads the specimens that match the current search, filters and sort as a CSV file named specimens-date-time.csv. The columns are ID, status, type, container, amount and unit, participant and collection codes, parent ID and derivation kind, collected, processing and registered times in UTC, custodian user name (blank while distributed), checked-out and on-hold (yes or no) and location. Status is written as its code: available, exhausted, disposed or distributed. Cells that start with =, +, - or @ are prefixed with an apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run them. An export may hold at most 10,000 specimens; a larger result is refused with a message to narrow the filters. If the filters are invalid you return here with an error. Each download is logged with who made it, how many rows and the filters used.

items.label: Print labels
items.description: Tick the boxes of the specimens on this page (the box in the heading selects the whole page), then choose Print labels to open the label preview. The counter shows how many are selected. Selection applies to the current page only. Up to 200 labels can be previewed at a time.

items.label: Row link
items.description: Opens the specimen record.

sections.title: Empty and error states
paragraphs: Before any specimen exists the page says “No specimens registered yet” and, for roles that may register, offers Register specimen. With filters that match nothing it says “Nothing matches these filters” with a way to clear them. An unsupported rows-per-page value is refused with “Invalid page size”; choose 25, 50 or 100.
